headline: Nvidia now carries more weight in a major global stock index than Japan does, yet The Irish Times says its shares are modestly valued against its earnings.
score_reason: Pool score 6 kept: read in full, figures are specific, but 'bigger than Japan' refers to index weight and the valuation case is the paper's argument.
importance_line: What changed is that one chipmaker now outweighs Japan in a global stock index, which matters first to savers whose pension and index funds lean heavily on Nvidia, then to fund managers, then to Nvidia itself, and the doubt is that the paper's case that the shares are not expensive rests on analysts' earnings forecasts holding up.
summary: The Irish Times reports that Nvidia, the world's most valuable company, has set a new record high after 96 trading days and now makes up 5.2% of the MSCI All Country World Index (a benchmark of stocks from around the world), slightly more than Japan and more than any country except the United States. The paper argues that Nvidia is still not obviously expensive, since its shares trade on about 15 times estimated earnings, according to Finviz, cheaper than 295 companies in the S&P 500 index, and that the company acts as if they are reasonably priced, having authorised a record $150 billion extra share buyback two weeks ago, as our 29 Sep 2026 edition reported.
notes: Read from the pre-fetched full text. 'Bigger than Japan' means Nvidia's weight in the MSCI All Country World Index, not Japan's economy. The extracted text shows no wire credit, so The Irish Times is credited as published.
